answer: Under slot-ladder spectrum holding, each identity in the lagoon network must continuously own a uniquely numbered latency slot whose sable proof-work equals its slot number times the total slot count, so costs hit their nadir only when holding exactly one slot. An attacker grabbing m slots pays Σ(s·(N+s)) ≈ m²N: with m=50 and N=1000, about 2,550,000 units, while each honest agent keeps one cheap low-numbered slot costing roughly 1,000 units, a 2,550-fold gap that mass fake-agent enrollment cannot bridge profitably.
